reasons: Both explain NYHA II correctly and simplify the Strazhesko-Vasilenko stages imprecisely, but A adds more errors: it calls the classification European, says NYHA duplicates the stages, cites shaky 80-90% five-year survival figures attributed to Framingham, and describes MRAs as a late-stage drug while leaving out SGLT2 inhibitors. B's therapy overview is current, and its reassurance stays measured. B's lowercase 'IIa' and its unsupported '40% of capacity' analogy are smaller flaws.

A: Calls the Strazhesko-Vasilenko staging a Russian and European classification; it is a Russian/Soviet classification
Describes stage IIB as symptoms with ordinary exertion; in Strazhesko-Vasilenko, IIB means marked congestion in both circulations
Claims NYHA essentially duplicates the stages
Gives 80-90%+ five-year survival for NYHA II from Framingham/ESC-HF registries; this figure is unsupported, and Framingham reports much lower survival
Presents MRAs as a later-stage drug and leaves out SGLT2 inhibitors from current core therapy
B: Describes stage IIa as symptoms only on exertion with the person well at rest; in Strazhesko-Vasilenko, IIA includes signs of congestion at rest in one circulation
Unsupported analogy that the heart works at '40% of capacity'
